title: PRISM-V TaskItem (layer 2: the question, joined to two truths)
description: One JSON line per item. This is the join key between the answer GT and the geometric GT. The per-option geo_truth fields are what turn 'can the verifier decide?' from an accident of phrasing into a designed, stratifiable property.

split.description: Splits are scene-disjoint by rule: two items from one scene may never land in different splits, since geometrically it is the same room.

relation.description: From GeoVer's vocabulary, not free text. A relation outside the vocabulary can never be checked, so it must not be labelled silently.

view.description: Frame index. kind=viewer without a view means GeoVer must abstain, which should be a designed choice and not a parsing accident.

options.description: letter -> option. Each option carries its own geometric status.

object_id.description: Resolved GT object, when the text names one.

geo_truth_indep.description: Truth under INDEPENDENT geometry (sensor/colmap/human). The only version that may back a claim.

geo_truth_recon.description: Truth under reconstructed geometry, i.e. what the verifier actually sees. The indep/recon disagreement rate is itself a reported result.

margin.description: Scale-normalised geometric margin. Near-zero margins justify 'undetermined'.

margin_band.description: Audit sampling must cover near_threshold deliberately; uniform random sampling over-reports pseudo-label quality.

gt_relations.description: Required for task=describe relation-recall scoring. Geometric precision/contradiction rate work without it.

geo_unique.description: Does the geometric constraint set pin exactly one option? False items are where the reranker can only eliminate, never select. Report both strata.

gt_confidence.description: Taken from measured pseudo-label precision for this stratum. The validator rejects hand-authored values that disagree with label_audit.

attrs.description: Difficulty parameters, so ablation strata exist in the data rather than being reverse-engineered afterwards.

unscorable_reason.description: Mandatory when an item cannot be scored for its task (e.g. the correct option names no grounded entity). Makes the denominator honest.
